key_insight: Machine-learned molecular dynamics predicts that about 0.5% biaxial tensile strain drives MAPbI₃ from tetragonal to cubic at 300 K.
engineering_relevance: Finite-temperature strain modeling can guide epitaxial perovskite design to stabilize target phases and tune photovoltaic absorber band gaps.
method: Train machine-learned force fields on-the-fly using DFT.
Run nanosecond bulk and free-standing slab simulations with fixed in-plane lattice vectors.
Track lattice symmetry, octahedral tilts, molecular orientations, and snapshot-averaged band gaps.
evidence_signal: The predicted transition agrees with MAPbI₃-on-KCl experiments, while snapshot-averaged band gaps reproduce the experimental tensile-strain blue shift that static averaged structures miss.
watch_item: Free-standing slabs do not explicitly capture substrate interfaces, so interface-specific effects require further validation.
paper_title: Strain-Induced Tetragonal-to-Cubic Transition in MAPbI$_3$ from Machine-Learned Molecular Dynamics
